known_gap.reason: DX20 cross-references ch. 154, and the algorithmic ordinance's body heading reads § 154-8. The codified text (code publisher pages D033/D034) is link-only, so the codified section number and any other ch. 154 rental rules are not captured.

value: Newly constructed multiple dwellings certified exempt by the Rent Control Board, for the shorter of the initial mortgage amortization period or 30 years
Dwellings vacant for at least 18 months (or already vacant) and substantially rehabilitated at a cost above 50% of fair market value, exempt for 5 years on Board determination
Units rehabilitated under Federal/State Rental Rehabilitation Programs receiving Section 8 subsidies or Federal housing vouchers, during program tenure
Units under a landlord contract with a governmental agency that regulates rent and supersedes city authority

evidence_corrections.before: Civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation; each month and each unit is a separate violation; Competitor Data = nonpublic data less than 90 days old; mandatory attorney's fees to a prevailing City Attorney or tenant
evidence_corrections.after: Ban on selling or using coordinated pricing algorithms to set rents or occupancy levels

evidence_corrections.before:
Chart A (7/1/2026-6/30/2027), per unit:
- Eligible: $11,000 (<3 yrs) / $14,400 (3+ yrs or low income)
- Qualified: $23,150 / $27,400
- Mom & Pop, owner or family occupancy only: $10,550 eligible / $21,250 qualified
Amounts increase every July 1.
Other terms:
- relocation paid within 15 days
- Declaration of Intent to Evict filed before notice
- notice copy filed with LAHD within 3 business days
- 30/60-day notice (120 days or 1-year extension for some)
- $75 owner/relative/manager occupancy declaration fee
- nonpayment eviction only above FMR (from 3/27/2023)
- Right to Counsel notice from 8/20/2025
evidence_corrections.after: Eviction only for an RSO just cause; no-fault evictions require relocation assistance

evidence_corrections.before: Notice to Quit periods: 3 days (disorderly conduct, damage, employment end, criminal offenses); 1 month (rule/lease breach, rent increase, lease changes, habitual late payment); 2 months (post-conversion/small-building owner or buyer occupancy); 3 months (health and safety removal); 18 months (retirement from residential use); 3 years (conversion). Relocation assistance for illegal occupancy: 6x monthly rent.
evidence_corrections.after: Eviction or nonrenewal only for a statutory good cause
Ban on landlord use of algorithmic rent coordination services; fines up to $2,000 per day

evidence_corrections.before: Administrative fines of $1,000 to $10,000 per violation; civil damages of actual damages or 3x one month's rent; punitive damages; attorneys' fees and costs; injunctive relief
evidence_corrections.after: No criminal-history inquiries or use in rental housing decisions

evidence_corrections.before: Penalties on conviction, one or more of: N.J.S.A. 40:49-5 penalties; fine up to $2,000; community service up to 90 days. Nonpublic competitor information = data less than 365 days old and not publicly available at no cost.
evidence_corrections.after: Ban on software, algorithms or data-sharing platforms that coordinate rents, lease terms or occupancy
No eviction, substantial lease change or refusal to renew in retaliation for protected tenant activity
Relocation assistance required when a rental property is demolished or converted

evidence_corrections.before: Chart B (7/1/2026-6/30/2027): Extremely Low $115,480; Very Low $96,750; Low $87,450; above low income per Chart A. Penalties from $250,000 per displaced unit. RSO/JCO base amounts paid within 15 days.
evidence_corrections.after: Protected-unit demolition requires relocation, notice and occupant protections; the highest applicable state or city relocation amount must be paid

evidence_corrections.before: Civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation; each month and each property is a separate violation; prevailing tenant recovers costs and attorney's fees; effective 30 days after final passage
evidence_corrections.after: Ban on providing or using algorithmic devices that set rents or occupancy from nonpublic competitor data

evidence_corrections.before: Civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation (per month, per law-firm alert) plus attorney's fees; private tenant action; effective April 2, 2026
evidence_corrections.after: Ban on selling, licensing, providing or using algorithmic rent-setting software for residential rentals
